title: A Wreck for the Compass
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the northern range, bush pilot Dominic Delacroix is the last person to have seen them alive — and the only one who can reach the crash site before the first snows seal the passes. What he finds is no accident: the team had discovered that the mining concession propping up the town's economy was built on falsified permits and buried deaths, and someone wants that discovery to stay lost. Joined by the survey leader's estranged daughter and a disgraced former Mountie turned trapper, Dominic must fly, hike, and outlast a hired killer across the range before the concession permits expire and the evidence — like the wilderness itself — forgets everything. The story ends at a tribunal hearing where testimony smuggled out on film forces the permit revoked, though justice costs them one of their own.
about_author: Vesper Fairweather spent a decade working seasonal jobs in remote fly-in communities before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and for heroes who find family in the unlikeliest cockpits and camps.

chapters.title: Fuel, Ice, and Rumors
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes his world: the fragile economics of bush flying, the town of Caribou Bend dependent on the Meridian Mining concession, and the rumors he carries like cargo. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness; he belongs to the sky but not to anyone.

chapters.title: The Last Coordinates
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He flies the survey team — four geologists led by Elena Marsh — to a high plateau, noting odd questions they ask about old mine shafts. Two days later, their scheduled pickup finds an empty camp: gear intact, no tracks, radio dead. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Ground Search
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Official searchers comb the plateau and find nothing; the company quietly discourages further effort, citing weather. Dominic notices boot prints deliberately erased and a burned document fragment. Emotional beat: the first suspicion that the wilderness didn't take these people — someone did.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Came North
chapters.summary: Nadia Marsh's POV. Elena's estranged daughter arrives by mail plane, furious at the official 'misadventure' verdict and at her mother for dying before reconciliation. She corners Dominic with her mother's last letter hinting at 'numbers that don't add.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: An Old Warrant
chapters.summary: Silas Crowe's POV. The disgraced ex-Mountie, now trapping alone, recognizes the burn pattern on the document from a case that ended his career — the same corporate signature, ten years ago. He approaches Dominic warily. Emotional beat: shame meeting a second chance it doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Hangar Fire
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Someone torches Dominic's hangar, destroying his logbooks and nearly him. The message is clear: stop looking. Instead he and Nadia reconstruct Elena's flight notes from memory. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into defiance; the found trio forms around shared arson.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Don't Add To
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Decoding Elena's letter against public permit filings reveals the concession's ore estimates were fabricated over a mass casualty at the old underground workings — covered up a decade ago, now being repeated. Emotional beat: horror that the past isn't past, it's load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Company fixer Aldous Vane offers Dominic a lucrative contract and veiled threats, revealing the company knows exactly what Elena found. Dominic plays along to buy time. Emotional beat: the seductive pull of safety versus the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: Crowe's Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas tells the full story of the case that broke him: he took a payoff to bury evidence, and the buried evidence was bodies. He gives them the location of his old informant — inside the range. Emotional beat: guilt offered as fuel, not absolution.

chapters.title: Loading for Winter
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Preparations: fuel caches, survival gear, Nadia insisting on coming despite zero field experience, Silas bringing a rifle and old maps. Vane watches them load. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; three broken people choosing each other as crew.

chapters.title: Over the Range
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The flight through deteriorating weather, engine trouble forcing a landing on a frozen lake short of the plateau. They continue on foot. Emotional beat: awe and terror of the landscape; the wilderness forgives nothing, and it's watching.

chapters.title: The Empty Cabin
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. At a trapline cabin they find signs Elena's team passed through weeks ago — and a fresh set of tracks belonging to someone following them. First night watch in shifts. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear; the hunter has become the hunted.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A storm pins them down for two days; supplies dwindle; Nadia's frostbitten hands force hard decisions about turning back. She refuses. Emotional beat: friction and tenderness — the group becomes a family precisely when it would be easier to quit.

chapters.title: The Informant's Grave
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the old informant's cabin and find him long dead, but his hidden cache holds photographs of the original cover-up and a map marking where Elena's team was headed: the sealed adit of the old workings. Emotional beat: grief for the dead man, and proof that patience outlasts power.

chapters.title: Tracks in the Snow
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Their pursuer — Vane's hired man, Rook — ambushes them; Silas is wounded covering the others' escape. They lose him in the timber but lose most of their food too. Emotional beat: fury and sacrifice; Silas insists he's finally paying a debt, not buying redemption.

chapters.title: The Sealed Adit
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. They find the survey camp inside the mine mouth: Elena's final report, core samples proving the fraud, and a diary revealing she sent a copy ahead — destination unknown. Then Rook's silhouette appears at the entrance. Emotional beat: triumph curdling instantly into siege.

chapters.title: Standoff Below Zero
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A tense standoff in the dark mine; Dominic talks while Silas flanks through a ventilation shaft. Rook is subdued but not before revealing Vane ordered the survey team's disappearance — they're alive, held at the company's remote camp until permits clear. Emotional beat: cold rage; mercy chosen deliberately over vengeance.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Concession
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Reunion with Elena and her team, weakened but alive, held at the derelict exploration camp. Escape plan: signal Dominic's backup floatplane on the far lake before the storm window closes and the permits expire at midnight. Emotional beat: joy braided with desperation; time is the true antagonist.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Out
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The escape march through deepening snow, Rook escaped and hunting them, Vane's men blocking the lake. Silas draws them off in a decoy run — and doesn't come back. Emotional beat: heartbreak and momentum; the family carries its fallen forward.

chapters.title: Last Light on the Lake
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The climactic flight: overloaded plane, failing light, Vane's truck racing the shoreline as Dominic coaxes the aircraft off the ice with everyone aboard and the evidence aboard too. Emotional beat: everything staked on skill, nerve, and the sky that never stopped being home.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. In Caribou Bend, the evidence reaches a tribunal before the permit expiry; survivors testify, Vane is arrested, the concession revoked. Elena and Nadia begin repairing what the years broke. Emotional beat: justice outside the law's original intention, delivered inside it at last; exhaustion and grace.

chapters.title: A Wreck for the Compass
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Spring: Dominic rebuilds the hangar, flies Elena's team back to the plateau to properly mark the old workings' memorial, and finds Silas alive at a trapline cabin, having crawled to shelter — choosing exile no longer. Emotional beat: belonging earned; the compass points not north, but home.
